do_more: Use the specific quote or lesson as the title (e.g., 'Know your enemy'), not a meta-description or summary.
Focus on tactical, actionable, or stoic-style wisdom (Sun Tzu, practical self-discipline) rather than broad philosophical overviews.
Keep titles under 15 words where possible; the top performers are concise and direct, while bottom performers are long, narrative-heavy, or use emojis.
Avoid emojis in titles entirely; the top 5 videos have zero emojis, while the bottom 25 all feature them.
avoid: Do not use 'in 60 seconds' or 'summary' framing in the title; it signals low value and feels like a textbook clip.
Stop using narrative hooks like 'He spent his youth...' or 'The man who...'; the algorithm and audience here prefer the direct insight over the backstory.
Avoid broad, abstract topics like 'Justice,' 'Morality,' or 'Ideal Government' without a specific, sharp angle or quote to anchor them.
short.title_style: Winning titles are direct, quote-centric, or present a single sharp tactical lesson without emojis or meta-commentary.
next_tests: Publish 3 Shorts using the exact title format of the top performer ('[Short Quote/Lesson]') with no emojis and compare VPD to the previous week's narrative-style titles.
Test a 30-second tight cut of a high-performing quote (like Sun Tzu) vs. a 42-second standard cut to see if brevity boosts retention on the 'war material' style topics.
Create a series of 3 videos on 'Stoic Tactics' using direct quotes as titles to see if a specific sub-niche cluster drives more serial viewing than random book picks.
